Evaluation: Analysis reveals a critical information asymmetry: while enemy absolute coordinates and the Overseer's (Agent 0) own absolute position are well predicted with communication (accuracy >0.9), the Roaches (Agents 1 and 2) fail to recover their own absolute X/Y coordinates (accuracy stuck ~0.2-0.3 even with communication). Variance across agents remains low because all three agents perform poorly on these dimensions—meaning the current protocol does not provide Roaches with the necessary reference to localize themselves. In contrast, without communication, Roaches already perform poorly, so the protocol is not bridging the gap.
Missing_Information_Hypothesis: The missing information is a common absolute reference point. The Overseer can infer its own absolute position from its wide vision (movement flags, enemy positions), but this estimate is not shared. Roaches cannot compute their own absolute because they lack a known absolute coordinate of any entity. They receive relative positions of enemies and allies, but without an anchor (e.g., sender's own absolute), they cannot resolve their own location. The current protocol broadcasts enemy relative positions and ally relative positions, but not the sender's own absolute coordinates. Thus, Roaches cannot triangulate their own position even when they see the Overseer or another ally.
Improvement_Suggestions: Modify the communication message to include the sender's own estimated absolute X and Y coordinates (relative to map center). Since the next protocol generation allows constructing messages from a 10-timestep observation sequence, compute these absolute coordinates by: (1) using the sender's movement flags and last actions over the sequence to integrate relative displacement, and (2) triangulating with well-predicted enemy absolute coordinates (which all agents recover from messages). For example, the sender can compute absolute as: self_abs(t) = enemy_abs(t) - enemy_rel(t) for any visible enemy, and average over visible enemies over the 10 timesteps. Broadcast these 2 values (X, Y) as additional fields. This directly gives Roaches a reference point when they have the Overseer or another ally in sight. Additionally, consider broadcasting the sender's own absolute velocity (ΔX, ΔY) over the last few timesteps to aid temporal alignment. These changes will enable all agents to consistently recover their own absolute positions, mitigating the information imbalance.
